question.text:
If A and B are square matrices of the same order, then $\operatorname{tr}(A B)=$

  1. $\operatorname{tr}(A+B)$
     
  2. $\operatorname{tr}(A) \operatorname{tr}(B)$
     
  3. $\operatorname{tr}(B A)$
     
  4. $\operatorname{tr}(A)+\operatorname{tr}(B)$
question.subject: Linear Algebra

question.text:
Which of the following vectors is an eigenvector for the matrix

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ll}
2 & 1 \\
0 & \frac{1}{2}
\end{array}\right]
$$

with eigenvalue $\frac{1}{2}$ ?

  1. $\left[\begin{array}{l}1 \\ 0\end{array}\right]$
  2. $\left[\begin{array}{l}0 \\ 1\end{array}\right]$
  3. $\left[\begin{array}{c}-\frac{2}{3} \\ 1\end{array}\right]$
  4. $\left[\begin{array}{l}1 \\ \frac{2}{3}\end{array}\right]$
question.subject: Linear Algebra

question.text:
The determinant of the matrix $A=\left[\begin{array}{cccc}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{array}\right]$ is:

  1. 3
  2.  -3
  3.  1
  4.  -1
question.subject: Linear Algebra

question.text:
Is 1 an eigenvalue of the matrix

$$
\left[\begin{array}{lll}
3 & 2 & 4 \\
6 & 6 & 0 \\
0 & 1 & 4
\end{array}\right]
$$

  1. Yes
  2. No
question.subject: Linear Algebra
